# ipe() Games

> 9 small games from ipe(). Short rounds, few rules, no ads. All 9 have their own site now.

play.ipe.rest is the portal for the games made by ipe() (https://ipe.rest/). It collects 9 games in one place and links to each game's own official site. All 9 games are coming soon: each has its own introduction site, and most are at the iOS TestFlight stage. None has had a full release yet: no store page or release date is set for any of them. This portal has no accounts or ads, collects only basic visit statistics through Google Analytics, and has no terms of its own (each game's site has its own terms). It has a journal with notes on turn-based games, killing-time games and how ipe() makes games.

## The games

- [Iltonggi](https://iltonggi.ipe.rest): A short, fast, classic territory-conquest strategy game set in Korea's Three Kingdoms era. Status: Coming soon. Platform: iPhone first. Pricing: No ads, no tracking.
- [Inkisle](https://inkisle.ipe.rest): A light island-conquest strategy game for your phone: send fleets between islands and tint the sea your color. Status: Coming soon. Platform: iOS first, Android alongside. Pricing: Planned: every round free · no ads · optional help items.
- [Sunmeld](https://sunmeld.ipe.rest): A merge duel against an AI opponent in one shared tub. Drop a stone, merge matching stones into the next stage, and score. Overflow the tub and you lose. Status: Coming soon. Platform: iOS and Android. Pricing: Free to try, one purchase unlocks everything, no ads.
- [Claimball](https://claimball.ipe.rest): A casual duel against an AI rival on a notebook grid. The tile where your ball bounces becomes your land. Miss, and you lose land. Status: Coming soon. Platform: iOS and Android. Pricing: Free to try. One purchase unlocks everything. No ads, no subscription.
- [Patchland](https://patchland.ipe.rest): A quick, offline territory game played with paper patches. Win land from six quirky AI lords, one region at a time, in three ways: Trace, Place and Spread. Status: Coming soon. Platform: iOS and Android. Pricing: No ads, no subscription.
- [Tottertop](https://tottertop.ipe.rest): A one-tap physics game. A swaying crane drops blocks, and you stack a tower that sways a little more with every block. Status: Coming soon. Platform: iOS and Android. Pricing: Free, with optional rewarded ads.
- [Moss Garden](https://mossgarden.ipe.rest): An idle garden for your phone. Plant eight kinds of plants, grow them, and gather the dew they leave behind. Status: Coming soon. Platform: iOS and Android. Pricing: Free, with optional rewarded ads.
- [Dusk Blocks](https://duskblocks.ipe.rest): Drop 3 pieces on an 8x8 board and clear lines. A calm, one-handed block puzzle at dusk. Status: Coming soon. Platform: iOS TestFlight now, Android later. Pricing: —.
- [Bottled Marbles](https://bottledmarbles.ipe.rest): Sort colorful marbles into glass bottles. A calm, clear sorting puzzle. Status: Coming soon. Platform: iOS TestFlight now, Android later. Pricing: —.

## How ipe makes games

- Short rounds that fit a break: A round should end in minutes, and closing the app should never cost you.
- Few rules, deep reading: If the rules don't fit on one page, the game is asking too much.
- A quiet app: No streak nagging, no ads, no accounts, and no tracking inside the games.
- Say what's true, including what isn't: If it's not released, we say so. If we haven't checked, we say that too.
- The AI plays fair: Comebacks come from the rules, not from a secretly weakened opponent.

## Journal

RSS: https://play.ipe.rest/journal/feed.xml

- [One new rule at a time](https://play.ipe.rest/journal/2026-11-12-one-new-rule-at-a-time/): Difficulty does not have to mean bigger numbers. Adding one rule at a time, as Inkisle plans to, teaches and challenges a player, and suits short rounds.
- [Three ways to claim land](https://play.ipe.rest/journal/2026-11-11-three-ways-to-claim-land/): Taking territory is one of the oldest ideas in games. Why it suits short play, and how three of our games use it in different ways: towns, islands and tiles.
- [Losing a short round](https://play.ipe.rest/journal/2026-11-10-losing-a-short-round/): Losing is part of any game with an opponent. Why short rounds make a loss cheaper, what makes a loss feel fair, and how our games try to keep it that way.
- [Pick a game by how much attention you have](https://play.ipe.rest/journal/2026-11-09-pick-a-game-by-how-much-attention-you-have/): Genre matters less than the minutes and the attention you actually have. A plain way to choose a short game, with all four ipe() games as examples.
- [A board you can read at a glance](https://play.ipe.rest/journal/2026-11-08-a-board-you-can-read-at-a-glance/): In a short game, the board has to explain itself in a second. Why color, shape and a plain grid matter, and how Claimball and Inkisle try to do it.
- [A game for one hand](https://play.ipe.rest/journal/2026-11-07-a-game-for-one-hand/): Many spare minutes come with a hand already full. Why portrait, one-thumb play shapes a game's design, and how Inkisle approaches it.
- [An opponent to practice against](https://play.ipe.rest/journal/2026-11-06-an-opponent-to-practice-against/): Playing a computer opponent is not a lesser way to play. What a good AI rival gives a short game: no waiting, no audience, and a ladder to climb.
- [One tub for two players](https://play.ipe.rest/journal/2026-11-05-one-tub-for-two/): When two players share one board, every move also changes the other side's options. A short look at why that makes a small duel interesting, through Sunmeld.
- [The first round is a welcome](https://play.ipe.rest/journal/2026-11-04-the-first-round-is-a-welcome/): A first round that is short and gentle lets a new player learn the rules without pressure. How Iltonggi plans its opening, and why we think it matters.
- [The part of the map you cannot see](https://play.ipe.rest/journal/2026-11-03-the-part-of-the-map-you-cannot-see/): Some turn-based games show the whole board, others hide part of it. Why a little fog can suit a short round, and what it asks of the player.
- [A good time-killer does not kill time](https://play.ipe.rest/journal/2026-11-02-a-good-time-killer-does-not-kill-time/): What makes a good casual game for spare minutes: it starts at once, you can leave any time, it ends cleanly, and nothing rushes or interrupts you.
- [Why turn-based games fit a break](https://play.ipe.rest/journal/2026-11-01-why-turn-based-games-fit-a-break/): A break has an edge you did not choose. Turn-based games fit that shape: stopping costs nothing, there is time to think, and a round can end cleanly.
- [How ipe makes games](https://play.ipe.rest/journal/2026-10-31-how-ipe-makes-games/): Five game design principles: short rounds, few rules, a quiet app, saying what is true, and fair opponents. How ipe's four games follow them.

## Languages

The site is available in 9 languages: English (en), Korean (ko), Japanese (ja), Spanish (es), Portuguese (Brazil) (pt-BR), French (fr), German (de), Indonesian (id), Vietnamese (vi). English is at the root; every other language lives under /<code>/ (for example /ko/, /ja/). English and Korean are written by ipe(); Japanese, Spanish, Portuguese (Brazil), French, German, Indonesian, Vietnamese are AI translations of the English original, marked as such on every page. The journal is written in English and Korean only.
